q: 1. Usefullness of plane table is enhanced by providing
explain: The Indian tangent clinometer, when fitted to the alidade, allows vertical angles and elevations to be measured directly during plane tabling, enhancing its usefulness.

q: 2. For the revision of an existing survey with the help of plane table we generally use
explain: Resection allows the plane table position to be located and oriented using already known points on an existing map, making it ideal for revising existing surveys.

q: 3. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distances directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade fitted with stadia hairs allows horizontal and vertical distances to be read directly (by tacheometric principles) without chaining, unlike a plain alidade which is only a sighting/ruling device.

q: 4. Locating the position of a plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as
explain: The three-point problem is the specific technique of orienting a plane table and fixing the instrument's own station by resection with reference to three known, plotted points.

q: 5. To orient a plane table at a point with two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted is
explain: The two-point problem is the special resection technique used to orient a plane table when only two well-defined but inaccessible points are available for reference.

q: 6. An advantage of plane tabling is
options: chances to miss details are less.
explain: Because plotting is done in the field itself while the ground is in view, there is little chance of any topographic detail being missed, which is a key advantage of plane table surveying.

q: 7. Which one of the following is known as instrumental error in plane table surveying?
explain: Non-horizontality of the plane table board is an instrumental (equipment set-up) error, as distinct from personal errors like defective sighting, orientation, or centering.

q: 8. Accurate centering of a plane table is done by
explain: A plumbing fork (with a plumb bob) is the instrument used to accurately centre the plane table exactly over the ground station point.

q: 9. The working edge of an alidade, is known as
explain: The straight ruling edge of an alidade against which sighting/drawing lines are drawn is specifically called the fiducial edge.

q: 10. Finding the location of the station occupied by the table, on the sheet by means of sighting to three well defined points whose locations have been previously plotted on the sheet, is known as
explain: This specific technique of locating the occupied plane table station using three known, already-plotted points is called the three-point problem.

q: 11. The two point problem and three point problem are methods of
explain: Both the two-point problem and three-point problem are specific techniques used to solve the resection problem in plane table surveying - determining the plane table's own position from known points.

q: 12. The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously, is called
explain: As established, plane table surveying is the unique method where field observation and plotting proceed together, simultaneously.

q: 13. The operation of turning the table so that all the lines on the paper are parallel to the corresponding lines on the ground, is called
explain: As defined earlier, this act of aligning the plane table so that plotted lines are parallel to the corresponding ground lines is called orientation.

q: 14. Spirit level in plane table is used for
explain: The spirit level fitted to (or used with) a plane table is specifically used to check and set the table perfectly horizontal, i.e., for levelling the table.

q: 15. Intersection is preferred to radiation when
options: it is not possible to measure any distance
the points are too far and invisible
explain: Intersection is preferred over radiation specifically when the points to be located are inaccessible, so their distance cannot be directly measured, requiring rays from two known stations instead.

q: 16. The strength of fix is poor when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the station is outside the great circle
the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle
the station is on the great circle
explain: In the three-point resection problem, the strength of fix is poor when the plane table station lies within the great circle (through the three known points) but outside the great triangle formed by them.

q: 17. The types of survey in which field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
explain: Plane table surveying is unique because the map is drawn in the field while the observations are being made.

q: 18. Plane table surveying is graphical method of surveying in which
options: field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
plotting is done later while records are taken in field book
explain: The primary advantage of plane table surveying is that the map is prepared in the field directly, eliminating the need for a separate field book.

q: 19. Orientation is the operation of keeping the table at successive stations such that
options: the position of the table at the station is parallel to the position it occupied at the previous station
the position of station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on ground
the table is brought in a horizontal plane
explain: Orientation ensures that every line on the paper remains parallel to its corresponding line on the ground.

q: 20. In the intersection method of plane tabling the number of stations needed to be set up are
explain: At least two known stations are required to create the intersecting rays for a single point.

q: 21. Resection is the method employed for
explain: Resection is specifically used to establish the location of the plane table on the map by observing known points.

q: 22. The two- point problem as compared to the three point problem is
explain: The two-point problem involves more steps and temporary setups compared to the three-point problem.

q: 23. Three point problem is concerned with
explain: This is a fundamental resection problem specific to plane table surveying.

q: 24. The triangle formed by joining the position of the known points on plane table survey is known as
explain: In the context of the three-point problem, the triangle formed by the three known points is called the great triangle.

q: 25. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to fiducial edge only for
explain: Errors due to non-horizontality are minimized or eliminated when the line of sight itself is horizontal.

q: 26. Which one of the following is not a personal error ?
options: the table not being perfectly leveled
the table not being perfectly central
the table not being perfectly clamped
explain: All listed items (levelling, centering, clamping) are under the surveyor's control and are therefore personal/instrumental setup errors.

q: 27. The method of plane tabling in which plane table is set only one station to take detail is known as
explain: Radiation involves taking rays and distances to all points from a single setup.

q: 28. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Radiation is the most efficient way to plot numerous nearby details once the station is established.

q: 29. Radiation method of plane table survey is the best suited when
explain: Since distances must be measured (usually with a tape/chain), it is best for short, clear paths.

q: 30. In plane table instrument for horizontal & vertical measurement without chaining
explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with stadia hairs for distance and a vertical circle for slope angles.

q: 31. Actually which is not the method of plane tabling ?
explain: Per the provided key, 'resection' is listed as the 'not' method here, likely referring to its role as a location tool rather than a detail plotting tool in this specific context.

q: 32. "Fiducial edge " is the working edge of
explain: The bevelled ruler edge of the alidade used for drawing rays is the fiducial edge.

q: 33. Which instrument is not used in plane table ?
explain: An altimeter is used for measuring altitude via pressure, not standard plane table plotting.

q: 34. The survey a small area which one of the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: For surveying a small area commanded from a single station, radiation is one of the most important (and simplest) plane table operations used for setting up detail plotting.

q: 35. An imaginary line joining the point of intersection of the cross-hairs of the diaphragm and the optical plane is called
explain: This imaginary line, joining the intersection of the cross-hairs with the optical centre of the objective, is by definition the line of collimation.

q: 36. The instrument used for accurate centering in plane table survey is
explain: A plumbing fork (with a plumb bob attached) is the specific instrument used to accurately centre a plane table exactly over a ground station mark.

q: 37. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Detailed plotting in plane table surveying can be accomplished using any of several methods - radiation, traversing, or resection - depending on the situation, so all of these apply.

q: 38. Intersection method of detailed plotting is most suitable for
explain: The intersection method, useful for locating inaccessible points from known stations, is particularly suited for hilly areas where direct distance measurement to many points is difficult.

q: 39. The resection by two point problem as compared to three point problem
explain: The two-point problem, requiring a trial-and-error graphical solution, generally requires more labour to solve compared to the more direct three-point problem method.
